what_happened: The agent told Sri at about 02:20 UTC that the retried "defect-discovery figure in the status keep rule" job was rejected. That was wrong. The rejected job was the critic-challenge mechanism. The defect-discovery retry, queued after the container restart, was still only proposed and had not run. The agent had named the job from the dispatch order and had not run athena status. No job work was judged bad.
cause: A person or agent reports on state without resolving what it refers to, and Athena does not guard it. Here the state was which job had been rejected. The agent worked from dispatch order, which is not a reliable map from position to job. Athena gives no check that ties a status claim to the current records, so the only guard is the agent's own habit of running athena status first.
other_causes: After the container restart, retries were re-queued under new items, so dispatch order no longer matched the original job names and the mapping was easy to get wrong.
Job titles in the status view are long and similar across related retries, which makes mix-ups easy.
open_hypotheses: Whether the container restart and re-queueing changed the dispatch order in a way that made the mismatch more likely cannot be confirmed from the given fields.
prevention: Add a default for agents and the person running Athena: before reporting that a named job was rejected, landed, failed or is running, resolve the job id and state from athena status or the job record. Never infer them from dispatch order, queue position or memory. State the job id with the claim.
proposed_request: Add a default to Athena's defaults set: before telling the owner or the person running Athena the state of a named job (rejected, landed, failed, running, proposed), resolve the job's id and current state from `athena status` or the job record, and quote the id in the report. Do not infer a job's identity or state from dispatch order, queue position or memory. Keep the default within the remaining token room of the reader set, and write it so its first sentence carries the rule, because only the first sentence of each entry is rendered. Add the CHANGELOG.md entry the changelog default requires.
